## What I changed

One file: `crates/reviewgraphen-ingest/src/rust.rs`. In `FunctionBodyVisitor::visit_block`, I added an arm for a block-local foreign module — `syn::Stmt::Item(Item::ForeignMod(nested))`. It hoists the names of the foreign block's `fn` (`ForeignItem::Fn`) and `static` (`ForeignItem::Static`) declarations into the block's `hoisted` set, exactly like a block-local `fn`/`static` item. Those names enter the block's *value* namespace, so a naked same-named call in the block is now shadowed (retained as a `RelationUnresolved` obstruction, not matched to the module-level function). Because the scope is pushed/popped per block, the shadow doesn't leak past the block, and because I only hoist the specifically-declared names, an extern block declaring *other* names doesn't block anything (the block is never marked conservative). I also extended the `LexicalScope` and `visit_block` doc comments to record the value/type-namespace rationale (a foreign `type` and the other foreign-item shapes bind no value-namespace name this resolver tracks, so their presence alone never blocks).

I ran `reviewgraphen-context visit_block` first (selector `visit_block`, the `FunctionBodyVisitor::visit_block` method) as required; it confirmed the target structure (the method, the `conservative_unresolved` state write, and the `use_item_bindings` helper it calls) and its declared information-loss surface before I edited.
